Best website reference sites

A practical shortlist of design-reference directories for finding website, UI, product, and interaction inspiration before building a new site.

By TurboApply4 min read
On this page
How to use reference sites Best reference site collection Rules for turning references into an original site

Website reference sites help teams find patterns for layout, interaction, mobile UI, typography, and art direction before a build starts. The useful workflow is not to copy a winning site, but to identify the job each reference does and translate that into an original, ownable implementation.

How to use reference sites

Start by naming the surface you are studying: hero, product section, pricing, case study, mobile navigation, form, animation, or editorial article. Then collect a few references for that exact surface instead of trying to copy one whole website.

Use references to define hierarchy, rhythm, interaction behavior, and quality bar. Replace all copy, assets, claims, code, and brand-specific motifs with project-owned material.

  • Collect references by component responsibility
  • Separate visual mood from UX behavior
  • Write an original implementation brief before building

Best reference site collection

1. CSS Design Awards

CSS Design Awards is useful for discovering polished marketing websites and interaction-heavy launches. The directory uses award categories, visual previews, and strong filtering so teams can study contemporary layout, motion, typography, and frontend craft.

2. Mobbin

Mobbin is useful for product UI, mobile flows, onboarding, settings, pricing, search, and app interaction patterns. The library uses screen collections, product categories, and practical interface examples so teams can compare UX decisions across real apps.

3. Awwwards

Awwwards is useful for high-end website inspiration, art direction, immersive motion, and editorial web trends. The site uses award pages, scoring, categories, and rich previews to show what current premium web design looks like.

4. Behance

Behance is useful for broader creative direction, campaign systems, branding, presentation style, and visual exploration. The platform uses project portfolios, creator pages, and visual boards so teams can study mood and storytelling beyond only live websites.

Rules for turning references into an original site

A good reference library prevents generic design, but it can also tempt teams into copying. Treat every reference as evidence for one decision: spacing, card anatomy, motion timing, typography scale, image treatment, or content hierarchy.

Useful search phrases include website design inspiration, UI reference library, web design awards, mobile app UI patterns, product website inspiration, interaction design examples, and portfolio design references.

  • Do not copy third-party code, copy, assets, or claims
  • Document which reference informed which surface
  • Verify the finished page by screenshots and measured browser behavior

Keep the next step practical

The best reference process improves taste without weakening originality: study the pattern, define the job, then build a site that belongs to the actual brand.
